steps.python_approach: pd.read_csv(csv_path) keeping the default RangeIndex (raw 0-based row position); rename columns with an explicit make.names helper (re.sub('[^A-Za-z0-9.]', '.', name)) so 'default payment next month' -> 'default.payment.next.month'. Never sort/reset_index.
df.columns = [c.lower() for c in df.columns], applied after make.names.
df.loc[df['education'].isin([0,4,5,6]), 'education'] = 4 on the numeric column, before the marriage recode (R order).

Positions 6..11 resolved (after id removal) to names ['pay_0','pay_2','pay_3','pay_4','pay_5','pay_6']; loop over these names: cast to float (R numeric) and df.loc[df[col].isin([-2,-1,0]), col] = 0.0. No iloc.

Keep the codes; the design function builds treatment dummies explicitly from the captured xlevels (sex [1,2], education [1,2,3,4], marriage [1,2,3]): column '<var><level>' = (str(code) == level) for every non-reference level. No get_dummies.
TARGET = 'default.payment.next.month' kept numeric 0/1 (R levels '0','1'); y = (value != first level '0') as float.
caret removed. No split code: fit() receives the train rows chosen by the harness from the R capture.

Explicit design matrix with '(Intercept)' first, then terms in R order. numpy IRLS mirroring glm.fit: mustart=(y+0.5)/2, eta=logit(mustart), deviance-based stop |dev-devold|/(|dev|+0.1) < 1e-8, maxit=25; weighted least squares via QR; SEs from the QR (R matrix) of the last iteration's weighted design, dispersion 1. coefficients() returns term/estimate/std_error with R names.
Build X_new with the same design function and captured levels; return 1/(1+exp(-X_new @ beta)); NaN where any input is missing (none in this data).

steps.r_construct: sex, education, marriage used as model inputs
steps.python_approach: Migrated faithfully without removal or change; recorded as protected attributes for validation.
